newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: U.K.'s Branson makes a comeback in music business.
newsitem.headline: U.K.'s Branson makes a comeback in music business.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson has said he wants his new record company to become a sixth force in the music business that can offer popular music bands an "artist-friendly" alternative to the conglomerates.

Branson launched the V2 Music Group on Wednesday, his first foray into the business where he first made his name since he sold Virgin Records to Thorn EMI for 560 million pounds ($940 million) four years ago.

"We hope to create a sixth force in the world in the music industry that can offer an alternative to the five major conglomerates and be more artist-friendly than perhaps the conglomerates have been," Branson said on Thursday night.
Global music sales total around $40 billion and the big five -- EMI, PolyGram, Sony, Warner and Bertelsmann -- account for some 70 percent of that.
During a visit to Lisbon, Branson said V2, an independent label, was looking to sign up new bands across the world and would assign teams of promoters to forward their careers.
"A record company is only as good as its artists," he told Reuters in a brief interview at the opening of a Virgin mega-store in Lisbon, now the biggest music shop in Portugal.

"Artists are only signed for three or four years maximum. If we have a team working around the world that the artists feel can promote a market for their product better than the big conglomerates, then it's quite likely that we can attract them."
Branson said confidence in Virgin's ability to promote music had in the past attracted artists such as the Rolling Stones, Genesis, Janet Jackson and Simple Minds to the label.
"We expect and hope that the same will happen again. But first of all we have to cut the ice with new bands and prove that we can do it," the multi-millionaire said.

Asked to forecast V2's sales in the first year of its operation, Branson said: "We've budgeted it on the basis of no success in the first five years and we've decided that any breakthroughs we'll be grateful for."
"But we've put aside enough money to make sure that we can set up and establish something which is on solid foundations for many years to come," he added.
V2 had already signed up a promising new band called the Stereophonics, Branson said.

"Let's hope they do as well as the first band we signed up for Virgin Records 20 years ago, which was Mike Oldfield," he said. Oldfield's Tubular Bells album became one of the best sellers of the 1970s.
Success continued throughout the 1980s with bands like Culture Club. International stars such as Janet Jackson and The Rolling Stones were part of Virgin's roster when it was sold.
Bands on the Virgin label now include Spice Girls, who are number two in the British album charts with their album Spice.
Branson joined the five Spice Girls in a dance routine on stage to celebrate his opening of a new shop in a former cinema.
